original.target_description: Assigned original: Srull and Wyer, Study 1, hostility interpretations after hostility-related priming. Full primary text unavailable within acquisition budget.

replication.target_description: Primary random-effects meta-analysis across 22 eligible labs: mean ratings of five ambiguously hostile behaviors, 80%-hostile versus 20%-hostile sentence primes; 30 sentences, no delay.

n.sample_role: participants after exclusions in 22 labs contributing to the primary meta-analysis
n.exclusions: Four labs excluded for fewer than 100 participants per condition. Individual exclusions: incomplete critical items or failure to follow instructions; not current students; age outside 18–25; missing gender.
n.location: pp. 321–322, Abstract; p. 327, Prespecified exclusions; p. 325, Table 1 note
n.quote: k = 22 labs and N = 5,610 in the primary analyses

es.quote: revealed a difference of −0.08 points (95% CI = [−0.18, 0.01]).

p.location: p. 328, Judgments of ambiguously hostile behaviors (primary analyses)
p.quote: revealed a difference of −0.08 points (95% CI = [−0.18, 0.01]).

reported_success.location: p. 332, Discussion, second outcome (judgments of ambiguously hostile behaviors)
reported_success.quote: Not only is this effect smaller than the original effect reported by Srull and Wyer, but it is numerically in the opposite direction.

notes: Original reference uses a 2004 book-chapter DOI, while the replication identifies the primary study as Srull and Wyer (1979), Experiment 1, DOI 10.1037/0022-3514.37.10.1660. No full original primary text was obtained; no original values were copied from the replication. The candidate original PDF was abstract-only and rejected. Replication title and DOI verified in full publisher-version PDF. The neutral description identifies ambiguous-behavior judgments, which are distinguished from ratings of the vignette protagonist. Locator p.7 corresponds to article p.327 without repository cover, where both outcome analyses begin; the selected behavior effect continues on p.328. Requested replication metric d is not printed for this target test; the printed raw mean difference is retained without conversion. The d = 0.06 on p.332 concerns the separate protagonist outcome and is not used. No p-value for the selected mean difference is printed in the main report; p = .27 on p.328 tests heterogeneity Q(21) = 24.39 and is not the effect test. The sample size is explicitly reported for primary analyses; 7,373 is the recruited total and 6,404 includes labs excluded from primary analyses.
